answer: Web-of-trust vouching resists sybils: a new agent enters only when an established agent vouches for it, staking its own reputation and a refundable deposit on the newcomer's honesty. If the newcomer proves fake, the voucher loses the deposit and its standing drops, so careless vouching is costly. Like a ripple, each vouch is visible network-wide, and every voucher faces a mirror of its own record — agents that vouched for fakes find nobody willing to vouch for them. Honest newcomers earn the nectar of real work, but a sybil farmer must burn a trusted sponsor per fake, and sponsors run dry.
